title.zh: 卷一百四十六 列傳第七十一 二李
title.raw: 卷一百四十六 列傳第七十一 二李 Volume 146 Biographies 71: Two Li's

sentences.zh: 李棲筠，字貞一，世為趙人。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun, courtesy name Zhenyi, was for generations a man of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun, whose courtesy name was Zhenyi, came from a Zhao family of long standing.

sentences.zh: 幼孤。

translations.literal: Orphaned in childhood.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents while still young.

sentences.zh: 有遠度，莊重寡言，體貌軒特。

translations.literal: He had far-reaching vision, was grave and sparing of speech, and his physique was lofty and distinctive.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed breadth of vision, was solemn and reticent, and cut an imposing, distinguished figure.

sentences.zh: 喜書，多所能曉，為文章，勁迅有體要。

translations.literal: He loved books, understood many fields, and in writing essays was forceful and swift with structural essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in learning, mastered many subjects, and wrote prose that was vigorous, swift, and structurally sound.

sentences.zh: 不妄交遊。

translations.literal: He did not make acquaintances rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful about whom he befriended.

sentences.zh: 族子華每稱有王佐才，士多慕向。

translations.literal: His clansman Li Hua often said he had the talent to assist a king; many scholars admired and turned toward him.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Li Hua often declared that he had the makings of a chief minister, and scholars flocked to admire him.

sentences.zh: 始，居汲共城山下，華固請舉進士，俄擢高第。

translations.literal: At first he lived at the foot of Gongcheng Mountain in Ji; Hua insistently urged him to enter the jinshi examination, and he soon was selected at the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: At first he lived at the foot of Gongcheng Mountain in Ji; Li Hua pressed him to sit for the jinshi examination, and he soon placed at the head of the list.

sentences.zh: 調冠氏主簿，太守李峴視若布衣交。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk of Guanshi; the prefect Li Xian treated him as a friend in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as chief clerk of Guanshi, where Prefect Li Xian treated him as an equal friend.

sentences.zh: 遷安西封常清節度府判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be secretary in Feng Changqing's Anxi military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as secretary in Feng Changqing's Anxi command.

sentences.zh: 常清被召，表攝監察御史，為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Changqing was summoned, Qiyun memorialized that he act as investigating censor and served as army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Changqing was recalled to court, Qiyun had himself appointed acting investigating censor and served as army marshal.

sentences.zh: 肅宗駐靈武，發安西兵，棲筠料精卒七千赴難，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was stationed at Lingwu and Anxi troops were mobilized, Qiyun selected seven thousand crack soldiers to go to the rescue and was promoted to attendant censor in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong held court at Lingwu and Anxi forces were called up, Qiyun picked seven thousand elite troops to march to the emperor's aid and was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 李峴為大夫，以三司按群臣陷賊者，表棲筠為詳理判官。

translations.literal: When Li Xian became censor-in-chief, he used the Three Offices to investigate officials who had submitted to the rebels and recommended Qiyun as judge for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian became censor-in-chief, he used the Three Offices to investigate officials who had yielded to the rebels and nominated Qiyun as judge for detailed review of their cases.

sentences.zh: 推原其人所以脅汙者，輕重以情，悉心助峴，故峴愛恕之，譽一旦出呂諲、崔器上。

translations.literal: He traced how each person had been coerced and defiled, weighing severity and leniency according to circumstances; he devoted himself to assisting Xian, so Xian favored and forgave him, and his reputation suddenly rose above Lü Yin and Cui Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He traced the circumstances in which each man had been forced into complicity, weighing guilt and mercy by the facts of each case, and gave Xian his full support; Xian came to cherish and forgive him, and his reputation soon eclipsed that of Lü Yin and Cui Qi.

sentences.zh: 三遷吏部員外郎，判南曹。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became vice director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently judged the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became vice director of the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent charge of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時大盜後，選簿亡舛，多偽冒，棲筠判析有條，吏氣奪，號神明。

translations.literal: In the time after the great rebellion the selection registers were lost and confused, with many false impersonations; Qiyun's judgments were orderly and clear, the clerks were cowed, and he was called divine in insight.
translations.idiomatic: After the great rebellion the appointment registers were lost and confused, and impersonation was rife; Qiyun's rulings were lucid and systematic, the clerks were overawed, and men hailed him as uncannily perceptive.

sentences.zh: 遷山南防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be defense and observation commissioner of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed defense and observation commissioner of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 會峴去相，棲筠坐所善，除太子中允，眾不直，改河南令。

translations.literal: When Xian left the chancellorship, Qiyun, implicated as one he favored, was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent; the public judged this unfair, and he was reassigned magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian left the chancellorship, Qiyun was punished as one of his favorites with appointment as junior tutor to the heir apparent; the public deemed this unjust, and he was reassigned magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 李光弼守河陽，高其才，引為行軍司馬，兼糧料使。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi, defending Heyang, esteemed his talent and brought him in as army marshal and concurrently grain commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi, holding Heyang, admired his ability and took him on as army marshal with concurrent charge of grain supply.

sentences.zh: 改絳州刺史，擢累給事中。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Jiangzhou, then promoted in succession to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jiangzhou and then promoted in succession to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 是時，楊綰以進士不鄉舉，但試辭賦浮文，非取士之實，請置五經、秀才科。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Guan argued that jinshi candidates were not examined through local recommendation but only tested on rhetorical essays and florid compositions, which did not reflect the true way of selecting scholars, and asked to establish examinations in the Five Classics and a xiucai category.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Guan argued that jinshi candidates were no longer chosen through local recommendation but were tested only on polished rhetoric and showy compositions, which did not reflect the true purpose of selecting officials; he proposed establishing examinations in the Five Classics and a xiucai category.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣議，棲筠與賈至、李廙以綰所言為是。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials to deliberate; Qiyun, Jia Zhi, and Li Yi held that Guan's proposal was correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the court to deliberate; Qiyun, Jia Zhi, and Li Yi agreed that Guan's proposal was right.

sentences.zh: 進工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 關中舊仰鄭、白二渠溉田，而豪戚壅上遊取硙利，且百所，奪農用十七。

translations.literal: In Guanzhong the fields had long relied on the Zheng and Bai canals for irrigation, but powerful kin dammed the upper reaches to seize profits from mills—nearly a hundred of them—and appropriated seven-tenths of the water for farming.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong had long depended on the Zheng and Bai canals to irrigate its fields, but powerful families dammed the upper reaches to run nearly a hundred mills and diverted seven-tenths of the water from agriculture.

sentences.zh: 棲筠請皆徹毀，歲得租二百萬，民賴其入，魁然有宰相望。

translations.literal: Qiyun requested that all be torn down; yearly tax receipts increased by two million, the people relied on the income, and he stood tall with the look of a future chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun asked that all of them be demolished; annual tax receipts rose by two million, the people benefited from the restored flow, and he bore himself like a man destined for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 元載忌之，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai envied him and had him sent out as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai resented him and had him posted out as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲仍旱，編人死徙踵路，棲筠為浚渠，廝江流灌田，遂大稔。

translations.literal: Drought continued that year; commoners died or fled in unbroken lines along the roads. Qiyun dredged canals and channeled the river to irrigate fields, and the harvest then became abundantly full.
translations.idiomatic: Drought persisted that year, and the common people died or fled in endless procession along the roads; Qiyun dredged canals and directed the river to irrigate the fields, and the region enjoyed a bountiful harvest.

sentences.zh: 宿賊張度保陽羨西山，累年吏討不克，至是發卒捕斬，支黨皆盡，裏無吠狗。

translations.literal: The longstanding bandit Zhang Du held West Mountain in Yangxian for years, and officials had failed to suppress him; at this time Qiyun sent troops to capture and behead him, his partisans were all wiped out, and in the hamlets no dog barked.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran outlaw Zhang Du had held West Mountain in Yangxian for years without officials overcoming him; now Qiyun sent troops who captured and executed him, wiped out his followers, and left the hamlets so quiet that no dog barked.

sentences.zh: 乃大起學校，堂上畫《孝友傳》示諸生，為鄉飲酒禮，登歌降飲，人人知勸。

translations.literal: He then greatly expanded the schools, painted the Biographies of Filial Sons and Brothers in the hall to show the students, and held village drinking ceremonies with ascent and descent of songs and toasts, so that everyone knew what to strive toward.
translations.idiomatic: He then greatly expanded the schools, had the Biographies of Filial Sons and Brothers painted in the hall for the students to study, and held village drinking rites with the prescribed ascent and descent of song and cup, so that all knew what conduct to emulate.

sentences.zh: 以治行進銀青光祿大夫，封贊皇縣子，賜一子官。

translations.literal: For his record of governance he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, enfeoffed as Baron of Zanhuang County, and granted an office for one son.
translations.idiomatic: For his administrative achievements he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, enfeoffed as Baron of Zanhuang County, and granted an official post for one son.

sentences.zh: 人為刻石頌德。

translations.literal: The people had a stone carved in praise of his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people erected a stone inscription in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 蘇州豪士方清因歲兇，誘流殍為盜，積數萬，依黟、歙間，阻山自防，東南厭苦。

translations.literal: The swaggering man of Suzhou, Fang Qing, took advantage of famine years to lure starving wanderers into banditry; they amassed in the tens of thousands, relying on the area between Yi and She, barricading the mountains to defend themselves, and the southeast was wearied and afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qing, a powerful man of Suzhou, exploited successive bad harvests to recruit starving refugees into banditry until his forces numbered tens of thousands; they held the mountains between Yi and She and the southeast groaned under their depredations.

sentences.zh: 詔李光弼分兵討平之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Li Guangbi to divide troops and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Li Guangbi to divide his forces and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 會平盧行軍司馬許杲恃功，擅留上元，有窺江、吳意，朝廷以創殘，重起兵，即拜棲筠浙西都團練觀察使圖之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the army marshal of Pinglu, Xu Gao, relied on merit, unlawfully remained at Shangyuan, and harbored designs on Jiang and Wu; the court, seeing the realm still wounded, was loath to raise troops again and at once appointed Qiyun supreme training commissioner and observation commissioner of Zhexi to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Xu Gao, army marshal of Pinglu, rested on his achievements, stayed at Shangyuan without authorization, and eyed Jiang and Wu; the court, still recovering from war, was reluctant to mobilize again and immediately appointed Qiyun supreme training commissioner and observation commissioner of Zhexi to counter him.

sentences.zh: 棲筠至，張設武備，遣辯士厚賫金幣抵杲軍賞勞，使士歆愛，奪其謀。

translations.literal: When Qiyun arrived he arrayed military preparations and sent eloquent envoys bearing heavy gifts of gold and coin to Xu's army to reward and comfort them, winning the soldiers' delight and love and wresting away their conspiratorial loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiyun arrived he made a show of military readiness and sent persuasive envoys laden with gold and cash to Xu's camp to reward the troops, winning their affection and breaking up their conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 杲懼，悉眾度江，掠楚、泗而潰。

translations.literal: Xu Gao grew afraid, crossed the Yangtze with all his forces, plundered Chu and Si, and then dispersed in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gao grew fearful, crossed the Yangtze with his entire force, plundered Chu and Si, and then broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 以功進兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: For this achievement he was advanced to concurrent censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 則又增學廬，表宿儒河南褚沖、吳何員等，超拜學官為之師，身執經問義，遠邇趨慕，至徒數百人。

translations.literal: He again enlarged the school buildings, nominated the veteran scholars Chu Chong of Henan, He Yuan of Wu, and others, promoted them supernumerarily as instructors, took the classics in hand himself to inquire into their meaning, and scholars from near and far rushed to admire him until his disciples numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He again expanded the school halls, recommended the veteran scholars Chu Chong of Henan and He Yuan of Wu, promoted them directly as instructors, took the classics in hand himself to inquire into their meaning, and scholars near and far flocked to him until his disciples numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 又奏部豪姓多徙貫京兆、河南，規脫徭科，請量產出賦，以杜奸謀。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that powerful clans in his jurisdiction often transferred their registration to Jingzhao and Henan to scheme to escape corvée and tax obligations; he asked to assess production and levy taxes accordingly to block such crafty designs.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that powerful families in his circuit often shifted their household registration to Jingzhao and Henan to evade corvée and tax levies, and asked that taxes be assessed on actual production to shut down such schemes.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 元載當國久，益恣橫，代宗不能堪，陰引剛鯁大臣自助，欲收綱權以黜載。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai had long controlled the state, growing ever more arbitrary; Emperor Daizong could bear it no longer and secretly drew in stern, upright great ministers to aid him, intending to recover the reins of power and remove Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai had long dominated the government and grew ever more overbearing; Emperor Daizong could endure it no longer and secretly enlisted stern, upright ministers to help him recover authority and remove Zai.

sentences.zh: 會御史大夫敬括卒，即召棲筠與河南尹張延賞，擇可為大夫者。

translations.literal: When the censor-in-chief Jing Kuo died, he at once summoned Qiyun and the Intendant of Henan Zhang Yanshang to choose who could become censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Jing Kuo died, the emperor summoned Qiyun and Zhang Yanshang, Intendant of Henan, to decide who should succeed him.

sentences.zh: 延賞先至，遂代括。

translations.literal: Yanshang arrived first and thus replaced Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang arrived first and was appointed in Kuo's place.

sentences.zh: 會李少良、陸珽等上書劾載陰事，詔御史問狀，延賞稱疾，不敢鞫，少良、珽覆得罪死。

translations.literal: When Li Shaoliang, Lu Ting, and others memorialized impeaching Zai for secret misconduct, an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate; Yanshang claimed illness and dared not interrogate; Shaoliang and Ting in turn were condemned and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shaoliang, Lu Ting, and others memorialized accusing Zai of secret wrongdoing, an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate; Yanshang pleaded illness and dared not conduct the inquiry, and Shaoliang and Ting were in turn condemned and put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝殊失望，出延賞為淮南節度使，引拜棲筠為大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply disappointed, sent Yanshang out as military commissioner of Huainan, and summoned Qiyun to be invested as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply disappointed, posted Yanshang out as military commissioner of Huainan, and summoned Qiyun to be appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 始，棲筠見帝，敷奏明辯，不阿附，帝心善之，故制麻自中以授，朝廷莫知也，中外竦眙。

translations.literal: When Qiyun first appeared before the emperor he presented matters clearly and argued sharply without flattery; the emperor's heart approved of him, so the appointment edict was issued from the inner palace itself—no one in court knew beforehand—and inside and outside the government stood in awe.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiyun first appeared before the throne he spoke clearly and argued forcefully without flattery; the emperor took a liking to him and issued the appointment edict from the inner palace without the court's knowledge, and the whole government stood astonished.

sentences.zh: 棲筠素方挺，無所屈。

translations.literal: Qiyun had always been upright and unbending and bowed to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun had always been upright and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 於是華原尉侯莫陳怤以優補長安尉，當參臺，棲筠物色其勞，怤色動，不能對，乃自言為徐浩、杜濟、薛邕所引，非真優也。

translations.literal: At this time Hua Yuan Assistant Commandant Hou Mochen Fu had been appointed Changan Assistant Commandant through the you quota and had to report to the Censorate; Qiyun looked into his background; Fu's expression changed and he could not answer; he then confessed he had been recommended by Xu Hao, Du Ji, and Xue Yong—not truly on outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Hou Mochen Fu, assistant commandant of Hua Yuan, had been appointed assistant commandant of Chang'an through the "outstanding talent" quota and was due to report to the Censorate; Qiyun looked into his record, Fu's face changed and he could not answer, and he confessed that Xu Hao, Du Ji, and Xue Yong had recommended him though he was not truly outstanding.

sentences.zh: 始，浩罷嶺南節度使，以瑰貨數十萬餉載，而濟方為京兆，邕吏部侍郎，三人者，皆載所厚，棲筠並劾之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao left the post of military commissioner of Lingnan he had presented Zai with rare goods worth several hundred thousand; Ji was then intendant of Jingzhao and Yong was vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel—all three were men Zai favored—and Qiyun impeached them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xu Hao left the Lingnan command he had sent Zai rare goods worth hundreds of thousands; Du Ji was then intendant of the capital, Xue Yong was vice minister of personnel—all three were favorites of Zai—and Qiyun impeached them together.

sentences.zh: 帝未決。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet reached a decision.

sentences.zh: 會月蝕，帝問其故，棲筠曰：「月蝕脩刑，今罔上行私者未得，天若以儆陛下邪？」

translations.literal: When a lunar eclipse occurred, the emperor asked the reason; Qiyun said, "Lunar eclipses warn that punishments should be rectified. Today those who deceive the ruler and pursue private ends have not been caught—could Heaven be warning Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: When a lunar eclipse occurred, the emperor asked its meaning; Qiyun said, "Eclipses warn that punishments must be set right. Those who deceive the throne and pursue private gain have not yet been brought to justice—could Heaven be warning Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 繇是怤等皆坐貶。

translations.literal: Thus Fu and the others were all condemned and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fu and the others were all condemned and demoted.

sentences.zh: 故事，賜百官宴曲江，教坊倡顐雜侍，棲筠以任國風憲，獨不往，臺遂以為法。

translations.literal: By precedent the emperor granted the officials a banquet at Qujiang with entertainers and mixed company from the Music Office; Qiyun, bearing responsibility for national standards of conduct, alone did not go, and the Censorate thereafter took this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the emperor gave the officials a banquet at Qujiang with performers from the Music Office in attendance; Qiyun, charged with upholding the state's moral standards, alone stayed away, and the Censorate thereafter made this its rule.

sentences.zh: 帝比比欲召相，憚載輒止。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly wished to summon someone as chancellor but, fearing Zai, always stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again the emperor wished to appoint a chancellor, but fear of Zai always stopped him.

sentences.zh: 然有進用，皆密訪焉，多所補助。

translations.literal: Yet whenever there was an appointment or promotion, he secretly consulted Qiyun, who gave much assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever he considered appointments, he secretly sought Qiyun's counsel, and Qiyun gave him much help.

sentences.zh: 棲筠見帝猗違不斷，亦內憂憤，卒，年五十八，自為墓誌。

translations.literal: Qiyun saw the emperor irresolute and unable to decide, and he too was inwardly troubled and indignant; he died at fifty-eight, having written his own epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor vacillate without resolution, Qiyun was inwardly troubled and aggrieved; he died at fifty-eight, having composed his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made minister of the Ministry of Personnel, with posthumous title Literary and Offering.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of personnel, with the posthumous title Wenxian (Literary Offering).

sentences.zh: 棲筠喜獎善，而樂人攻己短，為天下士歸重，不敢有所斥，稱贊皇公雲。

translations.literal: Qiyun delighted in rewarding the good and welcomed others' criticism of his faults; scholars throughout the realm looked up to him, and none dared speak against him—they called him Duke of Zanhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun delighted in encouraging excellence and welcomed criticism of his own faults; scholars throughout the empire looked up to him, and none dared speak ill of him—they called him the Duke of Zanhuang.

sentences.zh: 子吉甫。

translations.literal: His son was Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Li Jifu.

sentences.zh: 吉甫字弘憲，以蔭補左司禦率府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: Jifu, courtesy name Hongxian, entered office by yin privilege as warehouse clerk of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu, courtesy name Hongxian, entered office by hereditary privilege as warehouse clerk of the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，為太常博士，年尚少，明練典故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he was a Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; though still young, he was thoroughly versed in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign he served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; though still young, he was thoroughly versed in ritual precedent.

sentences.zh: 昭德皇后崩，自天寶後中宮虛，恤禮廢缺。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhaode died, since the Tianbao era the inner palace had been vacant and mourning rites had fallen into neglect.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Zhaode died, the inner palace had stood vacant since the Tianbao era and mourning rites had long been neglected.

sentences.zh: 吉甫草具其儀，德宗稱善。

translations.literal: Jifu drafted the full rites; Emperor Dezong praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu drafted the full ritual program, and Emperor Dezong commended it.

sentences.zh: 李泌、竇參器其才，厚遇之。

translations.literal: Li Bi and Dou Can valued his talent and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi and Dou Can admired his ability and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 陸贄疑有黨，出為明州長史。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi suspected he belonged to a faction and had him sent out as chief administrator of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi suspected him of factional ties and had him posted out as chief administrator of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 贄之貶忠州，宰相欲害之，起吉甫為忠州刺史，使甘心焉。

translations.literal: When Zhi was demoted to Zhongzhou, the chancellor wished to harm him and appointed Jifu prefect of Zhongzhou so he might vent his resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi was demoted to Zhongzhou, the chancellor wished to destroy him and appointed Jifu prefect of Zhongzhou so that he might take satisfaction in Lu Zhi's downfall.

sentences.zh: 既至，置怨，與結歡，人益重其量，坐是不徙者六歲。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he set aside resentment and made friends with Zhi; people esteemed his magnanimity all the more, and for this reason he was not transferred for six years.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived he put aside resentment and befriended Lu Zhi; people admired his magnanimity all the more, and for this reason he was not transferred for six years.

sentences.zh: 改郴、饒二州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chen and Rao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the prefectures of Chen and Rao.

sentences.zh: 會前刺史繼死，咸言牙城有物怪，不敢居。

translations.literal: It happened that successive former prefects had died; all said the yamen city had a supernatural creature and dared not reside there.
translations.idiomatic: Several successive prefects had died in office, and everyone said the yamen compound was haunted and dared not live there.

sentences.zh: 吉甫命菑除其署以視事，吏由是安。

translations.literal: Jifu ordered the overgrown grounds cleared and took up office in the residence; the clerks were thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu ordered the overgrown compound cleared and took up residence to conduct affairs, and the staff were reassured.

sentences.zh: 誅破奸盜窟穴，治稱流聞。

translations.literal: He executed and broke up the dens of treacherous bandits, and his governance was praised far and wide.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the lairs of bandits and criminals, and his reputation for good governance spread widely.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，以考功郎中召，知制誥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, Jifu was summoned as director of the Bureau of Evaluations and made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne, Jifu was summoned as director of the Bureau of Evaluations and entrusted with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 俄入翰林為學士，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the Hanlin Academy as academician and was promoted to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered the Hanlin Academy as academician and was promoted to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉闢拒命，帝意討之，未決。

translations.literal: Liu Pi defied orders; the emperor intended to attack him but had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi defied imperial orders; the emperor wished to suppress him but had not yet made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 吉甫獨請無置，宜絕朝貢以折奸謀。

translations.literal: Jifu alone requested that no troops be sent and that court tribute be cut off to thwart treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu alone advised against dispatching troops and urged that court tribute be cut off to frustrate Liu Pi's designs.

sentences.zh: 時李錡在浙西，厚賂貴幸，請用韓滉故事領鹽鐵，又求宣、歙。

translations.literal: At that time Li Qi was in Zhexi, lavishing bribes on favored courtiers, asking by the precedent of Han Huang to take charge of salt and iron, and also seeking Xuancheng and Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Qi held Zhexi, lavished bribes on the emperor's favorites, asked to take charge of the salt and iron monopoly by the precedent of Han Huang, and also sought Xuancheng and Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 問吉甫，對曰：「昔韋臯蓄財多，故劉闢因以構亂。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Jifu, who replied, "In the past Wei Gao amassed great wealth, and so Liu Pi was able to raise rebellion thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Jifu, who replied, "In the past Wei Gao amassed great wealth, and Liu Pi was thereby able to raise rebellion.

sentences.zh: 李錡不臣有萌，若益以鹽鐵之饒、采石之險，是趣其反也。」

translations.literal: Li Qi already shows the sprouts of disloyalty; if you add to him the riches of salt and iron and the strategic danger of Caishi, you will hasten his rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi already shows signs of disloyalty; if you add the wealth of the salt and iron monopoly and the strategic strongpoint of Caishi, you will push him toward rebellion."

sentences.zh: 帝寤，乃以李巽為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: The emperor awoke to this and appointed Li Xun salt and iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point and appointed Li Xun salt and iron commissioner instead.

sentences.zh: 高崇文圍鹿頭未下，嚴礪請出并州兵，與崇文趨果、閬，以攻渝、合，吉甫以為非是，因言：「漢伐公孫述，晉伐李勢，宋伐譙縱，梁伐劉季連、蕭紀，凡五攻蜀，繇江道者四。

translations.literal: Gao Chongwen had besieged Lutou without taking it; Yan Li requested to send out Bingzhou troops to join Chongwen in advancing on Guo and Lang to attack Yu and He. Jifu held this wrong and said, "When Han attacked Gongsun Shu, Jin attacked Li Shi, Song attacked Qiao Zong, and Liang attacked Liu Jilian and Xiao Ji—in all five campaigns against Shu, four went by the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen had besieged Lutou without success; Yan Li proposed sending Bingzhou troops to join Chongwen in marching on Guo and Lang to attack Yu and He. Jifu objected, saying, "When Han attacked Gongsun Shu, Jin attacked Li Shi, Song attacked Qiao Zong, and Liang attacked Liu Jilian and Xiao Ji—in all five campaigns against Shu, four went by the Yangtze route.

sentences.zh: 且宣、洪、蘄、鄂強弩，號天下精兵，爭險地兵家所長，請起其兵搗三峽之虛，則賊勢必分，首尾不救，崇文懼舟師成功，人有鬥誌矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover the strong crossbows of Xuan, Hong, Qi, and E are called the finest troops in the realm; contending for strategic terrain is what soldiers excel at. I ask that their troops be raised to strike the undefended Three Gorges; then the rebels' force will surely be divided, head and tail unable to aid each other, and Chongwen, fearing that the river fleet will succeed, will have men with fighting spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the crossbowmen of Xuan, Hong, Qi, and E are reckoned the finest troops in the empire, and seizing strategic ground is what soldiers do best. Raise their forces to strike the undefended Three Gorges; the rebels will be divided and unable to aid each other, and Chongwen, fearing that the river fleet will win the glory, will fight all the harder."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 礪復請大臣為節度，吉甫諫曰：「崇文功且成，而又命帥，不復盡力矣。」

translations.literal: Li again requested that a great minister be made military commissioner; Jifu remonstrated, "Chongwen's achievement is nearly complete; if another commander is appointed, he will no longer exert himself fully."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li again asked that a senior minister be made military commissioner; Jifu remonstrated, "Chongwen's victory is nearly won; if another commander is appointed over him, he will no longer give his full effort."

sentences.zh: 因請以西川授崇文，而屬礪東川，益資、簡六州，使兩川得以相制。

translations.literal: He therefore asked that West River Circuit be given to Chongwen while Li was assigned East River Circuit with the six prefectures of Yi, Zi, and Jian added, so that the two circuits could check each other.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore proposed giving West River Circuit to Chongwen while assigning Yan Li East River Circuit with the six prefectures of Yi, Zi, and Jian added, so that the two circuits could keep each other in check.

sentences.zh: 由是崇文悉力。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chongwen exerted himself fully.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chongwen gave his full effort.

sentences.zh: 劉闢平，吉甫謀居多。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi was pacified, Jifu's planning had the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi was suppressed, Jifu's counsel had played the leading part.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣使請尋盟，吉甫議：「德宗初，未得南詔，故與吐蕃盟。

translations.literal: Tibet sent envoys requesting to renew the alliance; Jifu argued, "At the beginning of Dezong's reign, before Nan Zhao was won, we therefore allied with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent envoys asking to renew the alliance; Jifu argued, "Early in Dezong's reign, before we had secured Nan Zhao, we allied with Tibet for that reason.

sentences.zh: 自異牟尋歸國，吐蕃不敢犯塞，誠許盟，則南詔怨望，邊隙日生。」

translations.literal: Since Yi Mouxun returned to allegiance, Tibet has not dared violate the border; if we truly grant alliance, Nan Zhao will resent and border friction will arise daily."
translations.idiomatic: Since Yi Mouxun submitted to the court, Tibet has not dared raid the frontier; if we renew the alliance now, Nan Zhao will grow resentful and border clashes will multiply day by day."

sentences.zh: 帝辭其使。

translations.literal: The emperor declined their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined the Tibetan envoys.

sentences.zh: 復請獻濱塞亭障南北數千里求盟，吉甫謀曰：「邊境荒岨，犬牙相吞，邊吏按圖覆視，且不能知。

translations.literal: They again asked to present maps of frontier forts and posts stretching thousands of li north and south in seeking alliance; Jifu advised, "The borderlands are wild and rugged, territories interlocking like dog's teeth; frontier officials checking maps back and forth cannot even know them.
translations.idiomatic: They again offered maps of frontier forts and posts stretching thousands of li north and south in exchange for an alliance; Jifu advised, "The borderlands are rugged and interlocking; frontier officials who pore over maps still cannot tell where the lines run.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃綿山跨谷，以數番紙而圖千里，起靈武，著劍門，要險之地所亡二三百所，有得地之名，而實喪之，陛下將安用此？」

translations.literal: Now Tibet spans mountains and valleys, mapping a thousand li on a few sheets of paper from Lingwu to Jianmen; of strategic strongpoints two or three hundred are lost—we gain the name of territory while in fact losing it; what use will Your Majesty make of this?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Tibet spans mountains and valleys and maps a thousand li on a few sheets of paper from Lingwu to Jianmen; two or three hundred strategic strongpoints are lost—we gain the name of territory while in fact surrendering it. What use can Your Majesty make of this?"

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔謝贊普，不納。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict thanking the Tibetan ruler and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent an edict thanking the Tibetan ruler and declined the offer.

sentences.zh: 張愔既得徐州，帝又欲以濠、泗二州還其軍，吉甫曰：「泗負淮，餉道所會，濠有渦口之險，前日授建封，幾失形勢。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yin had taken Xuzhou, the emperor again wished to return the two prefectures of Hao and Si to his army; Jifu said, "Si lies on the Huai, where supply routes converge; Hao has the strategic danger of Wokou; when we earlier gave them to Jianfeng, we nearly lost the strategic position.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yin secured Xuzhou, the emperor again wished to return Hao and Si prefectures to his army; Jifu said, "Si commands the Huai and sits at the junction of supply routes; Hao holds the strategic Wokou crossing. When we gave these to Jianfeng before, we nearly lost control of the region.

sentences.zh: 今愔乃兩廊壯士所立，雖有善意，未能制其眾。

translations.literal: Now Yin was installed by stalwart soldiers of the two wings; though he has good intentions, he cannot control his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was installed by the stalwart soldiers of the two wings; though he may mean well, he cannot control his men.

sentences.zh: 又使得淮、渦，厄東南走集，憂未艾也。」

translations.literal: If he is also given the Huai and Wo crossings, he will choke the southeast's routes of flight and gathering; the worry will not cease."
translations.idiomatic: If he also holds the Huai and Wo crossings, he will choke the southeast's lines of communication; our troubles will not end."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 中書史滑渙素厚中人劉光琦，凡宰相議為光琦持異者，使渙請，常得如素，宦人傳詔，或不至中書，召渙於延英承旨，迎附群意，即為文書，宰相至有不及知者。

translations.literal: Secretariat clerk Hua Huan had long been close to eunuch Liu Guangqi; whenever the chancellor's deliberation differed from Guangqi's wishes, Huan was sent to petition and usually got his way as before. Eunuchs transmitted edicts that sometimes never reached the Secretariat; Huan was summoned to Yan Ying to receive instructions, align with group opinion, and at once draft documents—chancellors sometimes did not even know.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Huan, a clerk of the Secretariat, had long been close to the eunuch Liu Guangqi; whenever the chancellor's decision differed from what Guangqi wanted, Huan was sent to petition and usually got his way. Eunuchs sometimes delivered edicts without going through the Secretariat; Huan was summoned to Yan Ying to receive instructions, align with factional interests, and draft documents on the spot—chancellors sometimes learned of decisions only afterward.

sentences.zh: 由是通四方賂謝，弟泳，官至刺史。

translations.literal: Thus he channeled bribes and thanks from all quarters; his younger brother Yong rose to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Through this he channeled bribes and gifts from all directions; his younger brother Yong rose to the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶當國，嘗一責怒，數日即罷去。

translations.literal: When Zheng Yuqing held power, he once rebuked Huan in anger; within days Huan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yuqing was in power, he once rebuked Huan in anger; within days Huan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 吉甫請間，劾其奸，帝使簿渙家，得貲數千萬，貶死雷州。

translations.literal: Jifu requested a private audience and impeached his treachery; the emperor had Huan's household audited and found assets of tens of millions; he was demoted and died in Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu requested a private audience and impeached his corruption; the emperor ordered an audit of Huan's household and found assets worth tens of millions; Huan was demoted and died in exile at Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「州刺史不得擅見本道使，罷諸道歲終巡句以絕苛斂，命有司舉材堪縣令者，軍國大事以寶書易墨詔。」

translations.literal: He also proposed: "Prefects must not visit their circuit commissioners without authorization; abolish the year-end circuit inspections to end harsh exactions; order the relevant offices to recommend men of talent fit to be county magistrates; for great military and state affairs use the imperial treasure edict in place of ink edicts."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed: "Prefects must not visit their circuit commissioners without permission; abolish the year-end circuit inspections to end harsh exactions; order the relevant offices to recommend men fit to serve as county magistrates; and for major military and state affairs use the imperial treasure edict in place of informal ink edicts."

sentences.zh: 由是帝愈倚信。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，杜黃裳罷宰相，乃擢吉甫中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, when Du Huangchang left the chancellorship, Jifu was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe, when Du Huangchang left office, Jifu was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent chancellor.

sentences.zh: 吉甫連蹇外遷十餘年，究知閭裏疾苦，常病方鎮強恣，至是為帝從容言：「使屬郡刺史得自為政，則風化可成。」

translations.literal: After more than ten years of setback in successive outside postings, Jifu came to know village and hamlet sufferings thoroughly and had long grieved that military commissioners were strong and arbitrary; now he told the emperor calmly, "If prefects of subordinate commanderies could govern on their own, customs and instruction could be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years of setbacks in provincial posts, Jifu knew firsthand the hardships of common people and had long deplored the overbearing power of military commissioners; now he told the emperor calmly, "If prefects in the subordinate commanderies could govern on their own, good government could take root."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，出郎吏十餘人為刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and sent out more than ten court gentlemen as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and appointed more than ten court officials as prefects.

sentences.zh: 自王叔文時選任猥冒，吉甫始簿其員，人得敘進，官無留才。

translations.literal: Since Wang Shuwen's time appointments had been rash and improper; Jifu first registered the roster of personnel, so men could advance in order and offices held no stranded talent.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Shuwen's time appointments had been careless and corrupt; Jifu first drew up proper rosters so that men could advance in due order and no talent was left idle in office.

sentences.zh: 又度錡必反，勸帝召之，使者三往，以病解，而多持金啗權貴，至為錡遊說者。

translations.literal: He also judged that Qi would surely rebel and urged the emperor to summon him; envoys went three times but Qi excused himself on grounds of illness, while he lavished gold on powerful favorites until some even lobbied on Qi's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: He also judged that Li Qi would surely rebel and urged the emperor to summon him; envoys went three times but Qi pleaded illness, while he lavished gold on powerful courtiers until some even lobbied on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 吉甫曰：「錡，庸材，而所蓄乃亡命群盜，非有鬥誌，討之必克。」

translations.literal: Jifu said, "Qi is a mediocre talent, and those he has gathered are desperate outlaws without fighting spirit; if we attack, we are sure to prevail."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "Li Qi is a mediocrity, and his followers are desperate outlaws without fighting spirit; if we attack, we are sure to prevail."

sentences.zh: 帝意決。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 復言：「昔徐州亂，嘗敗吳兵，江南畏之。

translations.literal: He added, "In the past when Xuzhou rebelled, it once defeated Wu troops, and the Jiangnan region feared it.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "When Xuzhou rebelled in the past, its troops once defeated the Wu armies, and the Jiangnan region feared them.

sentences.zh: 若起其眾為先鋒，可以絕徐後患。

translations.literal: If we raise their troops as vanguard, we can cut off future trouble from Xu.
translations.idiomatic: If we raise their troops as the vanguard, we can eliminate future trouble from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓弘在汴州，多憚其威，誠詔弘子弟率兵為掎角，則賊不戰而潰。」

translations.literal: Han Hong was at Bianzhou and greatly feared their might; if we truly ordered Hong's sons and younger brothers to lead troops in pincer support, the rebels would disperse without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong at Bianzhou greatly feared their power; if we ordered Hong's sons and brothers to lead troops in a pincer movement, the rebels would collapse without a fight."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 詔下，錡眾聞徐、梁兵興，果斬錡降。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Qi's followers heard that Xu and Liang troops were mobilizing and indeed beheaded Qi and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Qi's followers heard that Xu and Liang troops were mobilizing, beheaded Qi, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以功封贊皇縣侯，徙趙國公。

translations.literal: For this achievement he was enfeoffed Marquis of Zanhuang County and transferred to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was enfeoffed Marquis of Zanhuang County and promoted to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 德宗以來，姑息蕃鎮，有終身不易地者。

translations.literal: Since Dezong's time the court had indulged frontier military commissioners, and some held their posts for life without change of territory.
translations.idiomatic: Since Dezong's time the court had indulged military commissioners, and some held their posts for life without ever being transferred.

sentences.zh: 吉甫為相歲餘，凡易三十六鎮，殿最分明。

translations.literal: In a little over a year as chancellor, Jifu transferred thirty-six commands in all, with clear rankings of best and worst.
translations.idiomatic: In little more than a year as chancellor, Jifu rotated thirty-six military commands, with clear rankings of merit.

sentences.zh: 裴均以尚書右僕射判度支，結黨傾執政。

translations.literal: Pei Jun, as right vice director of the Secretariat with concurrent charge of the Bureau of Revenue, formed a faction to overturn those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun, as right vice director of the Secretariat with concurrent charge of the Bureau of Revenue, formed a faction to undermine the ruling ministers.

sentences.zh: 會皇甫湜等對策，指權強，用事者皆怒，帝亦不悅。

translations.literal: When Huangfu Shi and others answered policy questions pointing at powerful men, those in office were all angry and the emperor was also displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangfu Shi and others answered the policy examination by denouncing the powerful, those in office were furious and the emperor was displeased as well.

sentences.zh: 均黨因宣言：「殆執政使然。」

translations.literal: Jun's faction therefore proclaimed, "This was probably caused by those in power."
translations.idiomatic: Jun's faction spread word, "This was probably caused by those in power."

sentences.zh: 右拾遺獨孤郁、李正辭等陳述本末，帝乃解。

translations.literal: Right remonstrance officials Dugu Yu, Li Zhengci, and others set forth the whole sequence of events, and the emperor then understood.
translations.idiomatic: Right remonstrance officials Dugu Yu and Li Zhengci explained what had actually happened, and the emperor understood.

sentences.zh: 吉甫本善竇群、羊士諤、呂溫，薦群為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Jifu had long been on good terms with Dou Qun, Yang Shie, and Lü Wen, and recommended Qun as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had long favored Dou Qun, Yang Shie, and Lü Wen, and recommended Qun as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 群即奏士諤侍御史，溫知雜事。

translations.literal: Qun at once memorialized that Shie be attendant censor and Wen handle miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Qun immediately memorialized appointing Shie attendant censor and Wen to handle miscellaneous censorial duties.

sentences.zh: 吉甫恨不先白，持之，久不決，群等銜之。

translations.literal: Jifu resented that he had not been informed first, held up the matter, and for a long time no decision was made; Qun and the others bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu resented not being consulted first, held up the appointments, and Qun and the others bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 俄而吉甫病，醫者夜宿其第，群捕醫者，劾吉甫交通術士。

translations.literal: Soon Jifu fell ill; a physician lodged overnight at his residence; Qun arrested the physician and impeached Jifu for associating with occultists.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jifu fell ill; a physician stayed overnight at his house; Qun arrested the physician and impeached Jifu for consorting with sorcerers.

sentences.zh: 帝大駭，訊之無狀，群等皆貶。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly alarmed; investigation found no basis, and Qun and the others were all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly alarmed; investigation found no substance to the charge, and Qun and the others were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 而吉甫亦固乞免，因薦裴垍自代，乃以檢校兵部尚書、兼中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Jifu also firmly begged to be relieved, recommended Pei Ji to replace him, and was made acting minister of war, concurrent vice director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery, and military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu also firmly asked to be relieved, recommended Pei Ji to replace him, and was appointed acting minister of war, concurrent vice director of the Secretariat and chancellor, and military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 帝為御通化門祖道，賜御餌禁方。

translations.literal: The emperor saw him off in person at Tonghua Gate and bestowed imperial food and secret prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw him off in person at Tonghua Gate and bestowed imperial provisions and secret medical prescriptions.

sentences.zh: 居三歲，奏蠲逋租數百萬，築富人、固本二塘，溉田且萬頃。

translations.literal: After three years in office he memorialized remitting several million in overdue rent, built the Furen and Guben reservoirs, and irrigated nearly ten thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he memorialized remitting several million in overdue taxes, built the Furen and Guben reservoirs, and irrigated nearly ten thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 漕渠庳下不能居水，乃築堤閼以防不足，泄有餘，名曰平津堰。

translations.literal: The transport canal was low and could not hold water; he therefore built dikes and sluices to guard against shortage and release surplus, naming it the Pingjin Weir.
translations.idiomatic: The transport canal was too low to hold water; he built dikes and sluices to store water when scarce and release it when abundant, naming the structure the Pingjin Weir.

sentences.zh: 江淮旱，浙東、西尤甚，有司不為請，吉甫白以時救恤，帝驚，馳遣使分道賑貸。

translations.literal: The Jianghuai region suffered drought, especially eastern and western Zhe; the relevant offices did not request relief; Jifu reported that timely aid was needed; the emperor was alarmed and urgently dispatched envoys by separate routes to grant relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianghuai region suffered drought, especially eastern and western Zhe; the relevant offices failed to request relief; Jifu reported the need for timely aid; the emperor was alarmed and urgently dispatched envoys along separate routes to distribute relief.

sentences.zh: 吉甫雖居外，每朝廷得失輒以聞。

translations.literal: Though Jifu was posted outside, whenever the court had gains or losses he reported them.
translations.idiomatic: Though posted outside the capital, Jifu reported every gain and loss at court to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 六年，裴垍病免，復以前官召吉甫還秉政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Pei Ji resigned on grounds of illness; Jifu was again summoned with his former offices to return and hold power.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Pei Ji resigned due to illness; Jifu was summoned back to his former offices to resume power.

sentences.zh: 入對延英，凡五刻罷。

translations.literal: He entered audience at Yan Ying Hall and the session lasted five quarter-hours before ending.
translations.idiomatic: He entered audience at Yan Ying Hall and the session lasted five quarter-hours.

sentences.zh: 帝尊任之，官而不名。

translations.literal: The emperor honored and entrusted him, addressing him by office rather than name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored and trusted him, addressing him by title rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 吉甫疾吏員廣，繇漢至隋，未有多於今者，乃奏曰：「方今置吏不精，流品龐雜，存無事之官，食至重之稅，故生人日困，冗食日滋。

translations.literal: Jifu grieved that official posts were numerous—from Han through Sui none had been as many as today—and memorialized, "At present appointments are not refined, ranks and categories are bloated and confused, offices without duties are kept, and they consume the heaviest taxes, so the living grow daily poorer and superfluous eaters daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu deplored the swollen bureaucracy—from Han through Sui none had been as large as today's—and memorialized, "Appointments are careless, ranks are chaotic, idle offices are maintained at the cost of heavy taxation, the people grow poorer daily, and superfluous officials multiply daily.

sentences.zh: 又國家自天寶以來，宿兵常八十餘萬，其去為商販、度為佛老、雜入科役者，率十五以上。

translations.literal: Moreover since the Tianbao era the standing army has regularly been over eight hundred thousand; of those who leave to become merchants, enter Buddhist or Daoist orders, or are mixed into corvée levies, on average more than fifteen in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover since the Tianbao era the standing army has regularly exceeded eight hundred thousand men; of those who leave to become merchants, join Buddhist or Daoist orders, or are diverted into corvée labor, on average more than fifteen percent.

sentences.zh: 天下常以勞苦之人三，奉坐待衣食之人七。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm there are usually three who toil and suffer for every seven who sit awaiting food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm there are usually three who labor for every seven who sit idle awaiting their sustenance.

sentences.zh: 而內外官仰奉稟者，無慮萬員，有職局重出，名異事離者甚眾，故財日寡而受祿多，官有限而調無數。

translations.literal: Yet civil and military officials drawing salaries number no less than ten thousand; many bureaus duplicate functions, with different names and separated duties; thus wealth grows daily scant while recipients of salary grow numerous, offices are limited but assignments are countless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet civil and military officials drawing salaries number no less than ten thousand; many bureaus duplicate one another under different names, so revenue grows daily scarcer while salary recipients multiply, offices are limited but appointments are endless.

sentences.zh: 九流安得不雜？

translations.literal: How could the nine classes not be mixed?
translations.idiomatic: How could ranks and offices not become chaotic?

sentences.zh: 萬務安得不煩？

translations.literal: How could the myriad affairs not become vexed?
translations.idiomatic: How could government not become hopelessly burdened?

sentences.zh: 漢初置郡不過六十，而文、景化幾三王，則郡少不必政紊，郡多不必事治。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han there were no more than sixty commanderies, yet under Wen and Jing transformation nearly reached the Three Kings; thus few commanderies did not mean disorder in government, nor did many commanderies necessarily mean good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han had no more than sixty commanderies, yet under Emperors Wen and Jing good government nearly matched the Three Dynasties; few commanderies did not mean disorder, nor did many commanderies guarantee good government.

sentences.zh: 今列州三百、縣千四百，以邑設州，以鄉分縣，費廣制輕，非致化之本。

translations.literal: Today there are three hundred prefectures and fourteen hundred counties, establishing prefectures from towns and dividing counties by villages—expense is broad and control is light; this is not the root of achieving transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are three hundred prefectures and fourteen hundred counties, creating prefectures from mere towns and counties from villages—costly and weak in control; this is not the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 願詔有司博議，州縣有可並並之，歲時入仕有可停停之，則吏寡易求，官少易治。

translations.literal: I wish that the relevant offices be ordered to deliberate broadly: where prefectures and counties can be merged, merge them; where annual entry into office can be suspended, suspend it—then officials will be few and easy to find, offices few and easy to govern.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the relevant offices be ordered to deliberate: merge prefectures and counties where possible, suspend annual recruitment where possible—then officials will be fewer and easier to find, offices fewer and easier to govern.

sentences.zh: 國家之制，官一品，奉三千，職田祿米大抵不過千石。

translations.literal: By the state's system, a first-rank office received three thousand in salary, and field allotments and grain emoluments together generally did not exceed one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: By state regulation, a first-rank official received three thousand in salary, and field allotments and grain emoluments together generally did not exceed one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 大歷時，權臣月奉至九千緡者，州刺史無大小皆千緡，宰相常袞始為裁限，至李泌量閑劇稍增之，使相通濟。

translations.literal: In the Dali era powerful ministers received monthly salaries of up to nine thousand strings; prefects large and small all received one thousand strings; Chancellor Chang Gun first set limits, and under Li Bi amounts were slightly increased according to the lightness or heaviness of duties so that all could be mutually adjusted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era powerful ministers received monthly salaries of up to nine thousand strings; prefects of every rank received one thousand strings; Chancellor Chang Gun first imposed limits, and Li Bi later adjusted salaries slightly according to the demands of each post so that all could be balanced.

sentences.zh: 然有名在職廢，奉存額去，閑劇之間，厚薄頓異，亦請一切商定。」

translations.literal: Yet some held the name while the post was abolished, salary quotas remained while duties were removed, and between light and heavy posts thickness and thinness suddenly differed—I also ask that all be uniformly fixed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet some officials retained their titles after their posts were abolished, drawing salaries without duties, and pay varied wildly between light and heavy posts—I also ask that all salaries be uniformly fixed."

sentences.zh: 乃詔給事中段平仲、中書舍人韋貫之、兵部侍郎許孟容、戶部侍郎李絳參閱蠲減，凡省冗官八百員，吏千四百員。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Supervising Secretary Duan Pingzhong, Drafting Secretary Wei Guanzhi, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jiang to review and reduce superfluous posts; in all eight hundred redundant officials and fourteen hundred clerks were cut.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Supervising Secretary Duan Pingzhong, Drafting Secretary Wei Guanzhi, Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong, and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Jiang to review and cut redundant posts; in all eight hundred superfluous officials and fourteen hundred clerks were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 又奏收都畿佛祠田、硙租入，以寬貧民。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to take in the fields and mill rents of Buddhist temples in the capital region to ease the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized reclaiming temple lands and mill rents from Buddhist establishments in the capital region to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，義陽、義章二公主薨，詔起祠堂於墓百二十楹，費數萬計。

translations.literal: In Dezong's time the Princesses of Yiyang and Yizhang died; an edict ordered ancestral halls of one hundred twenty bays built at their tombs, costing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong's time the Princesses of Yiyang and Yizhang died; an edict ordered ancestral halls of one hundred twenty bays built at their tombs at a cost of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 會永昌公主薨，有司以請，帝命減義陽之半。

translations.literal: When Princess Yongchang died, the relevant offices requested the same; the emperor ordered half of what had been done for Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Yongchang died, the relevant offices made the same request; the emperor ordered half the scale used for Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 吉甫曰：「德宗一切之恩，不可為法。

translations.literal: Jifu said, "Dezong's indiscriminate favors cannot serve as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "Dezong's indiscriminate favors cannot serve as precedent.

sentences.zh: 昔漢章帝欲起邑屋於親陵，東平王蒼以為不可。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Zhang of Han wished to build walled dwellings at the tombs of his kin; the King of Dongping, Cang, held this improper.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Emperor Zhang of Han wished to build walled dwellings at the tombs of his kin; the King of Dongping, Liu Cang, held this improper.

sentences.zh: 故非禮之舉，人君所慎。

translations.literal: Thus unorthodox acts are what a ruler must be cautious about.
translations.idiomatic: Thus acts contrary to ritual are what a ruler must guard against.

sentences.zh: 請裁置墓戶，以充守奉。」

translations.literal: I ask that tomb households be limited and appointed to fulfill guard and maintenance duties."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that tomb households be limited in number to guard and maintain the graves."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾固疑其冗，減之，今果然。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I had long suspected it was excessive; reduce it—and now it proves so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I had long suspected it was excessive; reduce it—and you have proved me right.

sentences.zh: 然不欲取編民，以官戶奉墳而已。」

translations.literal: Yet I do not wish to take registered commoners—only official households to serve the tombs."
translations.idiomatic: But I do not wish to take registered commoners—only official households to maintain the tombs."

sentences.zh: 吉甫再拜謝。

translations.literal: Jifu bowed twice in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu bowed twice in thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「事不安者第言之，無謂朕不能行也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Whatever is not right, just speak of it—do not think I cannot act."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Whatever troubles you, speak of it—do not think I am unable to act."

sentences.zh: 十宅諸王既不出閤，諸女嫁不時，而選尚皆繇中人，厚為財謝乃得遣。

translations.literal: The princes of the Ten Residences did not leave their quarters, the princesses were not married in timely fashion, and selection of husbands all went through eunuchs, who had to be richly bribed with wealth before a match could be arranged.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of the Ten Residences never left their quarters, the princesses were not married in timely fashion, and selection of husbands all went through eunuchs who had to be richly bribed before a match could be arranged.

sentences.zh: 吉甫奏：「自古尚主必慎擇其人。

translations.literal: Jifu memorialized, "Since antiquity in marrying a princess one must carefully choose the man.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu memorialized, "Since antiquity emperors have carefully chosen husbands for their daughters.

sentences.zh: 江左悉取名士，獨近世不然。」

translations.literal: In the lands south of the Yangtze all chose famous scholars; only in recent times has it not been so."
translations.idiomatic: In the south they always chose men of distinction; only in recent times has this not been so."

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔皆封縣主，令有司取門閥者配焉。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict enfeoffing them all as county princesses and ordering the relevant offices to select men from eminent clans to match with them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict enfeoffing them all as county princesses and ordering the relevant offices to select husbands from eminent families.

sentences.zh: 田季安疾甚，吉甫請任薛平為義成節度使，以重兵控邢、洺，因圖上河北險要所在，帝張於浴堂門壁，每議河北事，必指吉甫曰：「朕日按圖，信如卿料矣。」

translations.literal: When Tian Ji'an was gravely ill, Jifu asked that Xue Ping be appointed military commissioner of Yicheng with heavy troops to control Xing and Ming; he also submitted a map of strategic points in Hebei; the emperor posted it on the wall of the Bath Hall gate; whenever Hebei affairs were discussed he would point to Jifu and say, "I daily consult this map—it is truly as you foresaw."
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Ji'an fell gravely ill, Jifu asked that Xue Ping be appointed military commissioner of Yicheng with strong forces to control Xing and Ming; he also submitted a map of strategic points in Hebei; the emperor posted it on the wall of the Bath Hall; whenever Hebei affairs were discussed he would point to Jifu and say, "I consult this map daily—it is exactly as you predicted."

sentences.zh: 劉澭舊軍屯普潤，數暴掠近縣，吉甫奏還涇原，畿民賴之。

translations.literal: Liu Yong's old army was stationed at Purun and repeatedly raided nearby counties; Jifu memorialized to return them to Jingyuan, and the people of the capital region relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong's old army was stationed at Purun and repeatedly raided nearby counties; Jifu memorialized to return them to Jingyuan, to the great relief of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 八年，回鶻引兵自西城、柳谷侵吐蕃，塞下傳言且入寇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Uyghurs led troops from Xicheng and Liugu to invade Tibet; along the border rumors spread that they would soon raid in.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Uyghurs led troops from Xicheng and Liugu to invade Tibet; along the frontier rumors spread that they would soon raid the border.

sentences.zh: 吉甫曰：「回鶻能為我寇，當先絕和而後犯邊，今不足虞也。」

translations.literal: Jifu said, "If the Uyghurs were to raid us, they would first break the alliance and then violate the border; now there is nothing to fear."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "If the Uyghurs intended to raid us, they would first break the alliance and then attack the border; there is nothing to fear now."

sentences.zh: 因請起夏州至天德復驛候十一區，以通緩急；

translations.literal: He therefore asked to restore eleven relay and watch zones from Xiazhou to Tiande to communicate urgent and routine matters;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked to restore eleven relay and watch stations from Xiazhou to Tiande for urgent communications;

sentences.zh: 發夏州精騎五百屯經略故城，以護党項而已。

translations.literal: and to dispatch five hundred crack cavalry from Xiazhou to garrison the old seat of the frontier command, solely to protect the Tangut tribes.
translations.idiomatic: and to dispatch five hundred elite cavalry from Xiazhou to garrison the old frontier command seat, solely to protect the Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 既而果邊吏妄言。

translations.literal: In the end it proved to be false talk by frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it proved to be false alarm raised by frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 六胡州在靈武部中，開元時廢之，置宥州以處降戶，寓治經略軍，居中以制戎虜，北援天德，南接夏州。

translations.literal: The Six Hu Prefectures lay within the Lingwu region; in the Kaiyuan era they were abolished and Youzhou was established to settle surrendered households, with administration lodged at the frontier command army, positioned centrally to control the barbarians, aiding Tiande to the north and linking Xiazhou to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Hu Prefectures lay within the Lingwu region; in the Kaiyuan era they were abolished and Youzhou was established for surrendered tribes, administered from the frontier command, positioned to control the barbarians, supporting Tiande to the north and linking Xiazhou to the south.

sentences.zh: 至德、寶應間，廢宥州，以軍遙隸靈武，道裏曠遠，故党項孤弱，虜數擾之。

translations.literal: Between Zhide and Baoying Youzhou was abolished and the army was remotely subordinated to Lingwu; the route was vast and distant, so the Tangut were isolated and weak and the barbarians repeatedly harassed them.
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhide and Baoying Youzhou was abolished and the army was placed under distant Lingwu command; the route was vast and remote, the Tangut were isolated and weak, and the barbarians repeatedly harassed them.

sentences.zh: 吉甫始奏復宥州，乃治經略軍，以隸綏銀道，取鄜城神策屯兵九千實之。

translations.literal: Jifu first memorialized to restore Youzhou, then restored the frontier command army, subordinated it to the Suibin circuit, and took nine thousand Shence garrison troops from Fucheng to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu first memorialized to restore Youzhou, restored the frontier command, placed it under the Suibin circuit, and stationed nine thousand Shence troops from Fucheng there.

sentences.zh: 以江淮甲三十萬給太原、澤潞軍，增太原馬千匹。

translations.literal: Three hundred thousand suits of armor from the Jianghuai region were given to the Taiyuan and Zelu armies, and Taiyuan's horses were increased by one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred thousand suits of armor from the Jianghuai region were supplied to the Taiyuan and Zelu armies, and Taiyuan's horse complement was increased by one thousand.

sentences.zh: 由是戎備完輯。

translations.literal: Thereby frontier defenses were complete and in order.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby frontier defenses were brought into good order.

sentences.zh: 自蜀平，帝銳意欲取淮西。

translations.literal: Since Shu was pacified, the emperor was keenly intent on taking Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shu was pacified, the emperor was keenly intent on recovering Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 方吉甫在淮南，聞吳少陽立，上下攜泮，自請徙壽州，以天子命招懷之，反間以撓其黨，會討王承宗，未及用。

translations.literal: While Jifu was in Huainan he heard that Wu Shaoyang had been installed and that superiors and subordinates were at odds; he volunteered to transfer to Shouzhou to win him over by imperial command and use counterintelligence to shake his faction; but the campaign against Wang Chengzong intervened and the plan was not used.
translations.idiomatic: While Jifu was in Huainan he heard that Wu Shaoyang had succeeded to power and that his followers were divided; he volunteered to transfer to Shouzhou to win him over by imperial command and use counterintelligence to divide his faction; but the campaign against Wang Chengzong intervened and the plan was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 後田弘正以魏歸，吉甫知魏人謂田進誠才，而唐州乃蔡喉衿，請拔進誠為刺史，以臨賊境，且慰魏心。

translations.literal: Later when Tian Hongzheng brought Wei back to allegiance, Jifu knew the people of Wei said Tian Jincheng had talent, and that Tangzhou was the throat and collar of Cai; he asked to promote Jincheng as prefect to face the rebel territory and also reassure Wei's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Tian Hongzheng brought Wei back to allegiance, Jifu knew the people of Wei admired Tian Jincheng's ability, and that Tangzhou was the throat of Cai territory; he asked to appoint Jincheng prefect of Tangzhou to face the rebels and reassure Wei.

sentences.zh: 烏重胤守河陽，吉甫以汝州捍蔽東都，聯唐、許，當蔡西面，兵寡不足憚寇，而河陽乃魏博之津，弘正歸國，則為內鎮，不宜戍重兵示不信，請徙屯汝州。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin held Heyang; Jifu held that Ruzhou shielded the eastern capital, linked Tang and Xu, and faced Cai on the west—with few troops it was not enough to deter the enemy; yet Heyang was the ford of Weibo; with Hongzheng's return to allegiance it became an inner command and should not be garrisoned with heavy troops showing distrust—he asked to move the garrison to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin held Heyang; Jifu argued that Ruzhou shielded the eastern capital, linked Tang and Xu, and faced Cai on the west, and with few troops could not deter the enemy; yet Heyang was Weibo's strategic crossing—with Hongzheng's return it became an inner command and should not be heavily garrisoned as a sign of distrust; he asked to move the garrison to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 後弘正拜檢校尚書右僕射，賜其軍錢二千萬，弘正曰：「吾未喜於移河陽軍也。」

translations.literal: Later Hongzheng was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat and granted twenty million in cash for his army; Hongzheng said, "I am not pleased about the transfer of the Heyang army."
translations.idiomatic: Later Hongzheng was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat and granted twenty million in cash for his army; Hongzheng said, "What displeases me is not the money but the transfer of the Heyang garrison."

sentences.zh: 及元濟擅立，吉甫以內地無唇齒援，因時可取，不當用河朔故事，與帝意合。

translations.literal: When Yuanji seized power on his own, Jifu held that the inner regions had no lip-and-teeth support, that the moment could be seized, and that the Hebei precedent should not be applied—the emperor's mind agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji seized power on his own, Jifu argued that the central provinces had no mutual support, that the moment could be seized, and that the Hebei precedent of indulgence should not apply—the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又請自往招元濟，茍逆誌不悛，得指授群帥俘賊以獻天子。

translations.literal: He also asked to go in person to win over Yuanji; if the rebel's will did not repent, he could direct the commanders to capture the bandit and present him to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to go in person to win over Yuanji; if the rebel would not repent, he could direct the commanders to capture him and present him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 不許，固請至流涕，帝慰勉之。

translations.literal: This was not granted; he pressed his request until he wept; the emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; Jifu pressed his request until he wept; the emperor comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 會暴疾卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: He then died suddenly of illness at fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He then died suddenly of illness at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 帝震悼，賻外別賜縑五百恤其家，自大斂至卒哭，皆中人臨吊。

translations.literal: The emperor was shocked and grieved; beyond funeral gifts he separately bestowed five hundred bolts of silk to comfort the family; from the great encoffinment to the final mourning cry, eunuchs attended to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and grieved; beyond the standard funeral gifts he bestowed five hundred bolts of silk on the family; from the encoffinment to the final mourning rites, eunuchs attended on the emperor's behalf.

sentences.zh: 吉甫圖淮西地，未及上，帝敕其子獻之。

translations.literal: Jifu had mapped Huaixi territory but had not yet submitted it; the emperor ordered his son to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had mapped Huaixi territory but had not yet submitted the map; the emperor ordered his son to present it.

sentences.zh: 及葬，祭以少牢，贈司空。

translations.literal: At burial he was sacrificed to with the lesser tai la ritual and posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial the emperor sacrificed with the lesser tai la ritual and posthumously appointed him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 有司謚曰敬憲，度支郎中張仲方非之，帝怒，貶仲方，更賜謚曰忠懿。

translations.literal: The relevant offices gave the posthumous title Respectful and Law-abiding; Bureau of Revenue director Zhang Zhongfang objected; the emperor was angry and demoted Zhongfang, changing the posthumous title to Loyal and Admirable.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices proposed the posthumous title Jingxian (Respectful and Law-abiding); Bureau of Revenue director Zhang Zhongfang objected; the emperor was angry and demoted Zhongfang, changing the posthumous title to Zhongyi (Loyal and Admirable).

sentences.zh: 始，吉甫當國，經綜政事，眾職咸治。

translations.literal: At first, when Jifu held power, he coordinated government affairs and all duties were well governed.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Jifu held power, he coordinated government affairs and every office functioned well.

sentences.zh: 引薦賢士大夫，愛善無遺，褒忠臣後，以起義烈。

translations.literal: He recommended worthy scholar-officials, cherished excellence without omission, honored the descendants of loyal ministers, and thereby roused righteous fervor.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended worthy scholar-officials, cherished talent without reserve, honored the descendants of loyal ministers, and thereby inspired righteous fervor.

sentences.zh: 與武元衡連位，未幾節度劍南，屢言元衡材，宜還為相。

translations.literal: He served in succession with Wu Yuanheng; before long Yuanheng was made military commissioner of Jiannan; Jifu repeatedly said Yuanheng had talent and should return as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession with Wu Yuanheng; before long Yuanheng was posted military commissioner of Jiannan; Jifu repeatedly said Yuanheng had the talent to return as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及再輔政，天下想望風采，而稍修怨，罷李藩宰相，而裴垍左遷，皆其謀也。

translations.literal: When he again assisted in government, the realm looked to his bearing with hope; yet he gradually nursed grievances—dismissing Li Fan from the chancellorship and demoting Pei Ji to a lower post were all his doing.
translations.idiomatic: When he again took up power, the realm looked to him with hope; yet he gradually nursed grievances—dismissing Li Fan from the chancellorship and demoting Pei Ji were all his doing.

sentences.zh: 李正辭晚相失，及與蕭俛同召為翰林學士，獨用俛而罷正辭，人莫不疑憚。

translations.literal: He fell out with Li Zhengci late in life; when Xiao Mian was summoned with Zhengci as Hanlin academician, he used only Mian and dismissed Zhengci—none did not suspect and fear him.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Li Zhengci late in life; when Xiao Mian and Zhengci were both summoned as Hanlin academicians, he used only Mian and dismissed Zhengci—everyone suspected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 帝亦知其專，乃進李絳，遂與有隙，數辯爭殿上，帝多直絳。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew he was arbitrary and therefore advanced Li Jiang; thus they had a rift and often argued in the hall; the emperor mostly sided with Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also knew he was overbearing and advanced Li Jiang; the two clashed and often argued in court; the emperor usually sided with Jiang.

sentences.zh: 然畏慎奉法，不忮害，顧大體。

translations.literal: Yet he was cautious and revered the law, did not harm out of jealousy, and looked to the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was cautious and law-abiding, did not harm others out of jealousy, and kept the larger interest in view.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺楊歸厚嘗請對，日已旰，帝令它日見，固請不肯退。

translations.literal: Left remonstrance official Yang Guihou once requested audience; the sun was already late; the emperor ordered him to come another day; he pressed his request and would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Left remonstrance official Yang Guihou once requested an audience; the day was already late; the emperor told him to return another day; he insisted and refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 既見，極論中人許遂振之奸，又歷詆輔相，求自試，又表假郵置院具婚禮。

translations.literal: Once received in audience he exhaustively discussed the treachery of the eunuch Xu Suizhen, then went through denouncing the chancellors, asked to be tried himself, and also memorialized to borrow the postal relay compound to prepare his wedding.
translations.idiomatic: Once received in audience he denounced the treachery of the eunuch Xu Suizhen, went on to denounce the chancellors, asked to be given a trial assignment, and memorialized to borrow the postal relay compound for his wedding.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其輕肆，欲遠斥之，李絳為言，不能得。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry at his frivolity and wished to banish him far away; Li Jiang spoke on his behalf but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry at his presumption and wished to banish him; Li Jiang spoke on his behalf but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 吉甫見帝，謝引用之非，帝意釋，得以國子主簿分司東都。

translations.literal: Jifu saw the emperor and apologized for the impropriety of having recommended him; the emperor's mind was eased, and Guihou was allowed to serve as director of studies at the National University on detached duty in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu saw the emperor and apologized for having recommended him improperly; the emperor relented, and Guihou was allowed to serve as director of studies at the National University on detached duty in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，政事堂會食，有巨床，相傳徙者宰相輒罷，不敢遷，吉甫笑曰：「世俗禁忌，何足疑邪？」

translations.literal: At first, when the Chancellery dined together, there was a great couch; tradition held that whichever chancellor moved it would be dismissed, and none dared shift it; Jifu laughed and said, "Worldly taboos—what is there to doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the chancellors dined together in the Chancellery, there was a great couch; tradition held that whichever chancellor moved it would be dismissed, and none dared touch it; Jifu laughed and said, "What worldly superstition is worth heeding?"

sentences.zh: 徹而新之。

translations.literal: He removed it and had a new one made.
translations.idiomatic: He had it removed and replaced with a new one.

sentences.zh: 吉甫居安邑裏，時號「安邑李丞相」。

translations.literal: Jifu lived in Anyi Lane and was at the time called "Chancellor Li of Anyi."
translations.idiomatic: Jifu lived in Anyi Lane and was known as "Chancellor Li of Anyi."

sentences.zh: 所論著甚多，皆行於世。

translations.literal: His writings were numerous and all circulated in the world.
