translations.idiomatic: He wrote extensively, and his works all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 前卒一歲，熒惑掩太微上相，吉甫曰：「天且殺我。」

translations.literal: A year before his death Mars occulted the Upper Chancellor star in Taiwei; Jifu said, "Heaven is about to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: A year before his death Mars occulted the Upper Chancellor star in the Taiwei constellation; Jifu said, "Heaven is about to take my life."

sentences.zh: 再遜位，不許。

translations.literal: He twice yielded his post; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He twice offered to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 子德修，亦有誌操，寶歷中為膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Dexiu also had moral resolve; in the Baoli era he was vice director of the Bureau of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dexiu also had moral integrity; during the Baoli reign he served as vice director of the Bureau of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 張仲方入為諫議大夫，德修不欲同朝，出為舒、湖、楚三州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhongfang entered office as remonstrance grandee, Dexiu did not wish to serve in the same court and was sent out as prefect of Shu, Hu, and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhongfang entered office as remonstrance grandee, Dexiu refused to serve in the same court and was posted out as prefect of Shu, Hu, and Chu.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 次子德裕，自有傳。

translations.literal: His second son Deyu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Li Deyu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 李鄘，字建侯，北海太守邕之從孫。

translations.literal: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was a grandnephew of Li Yong the prefect of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, courtesy name Jianhou, was a grandnephew of the famous calligrapher Li Yong, who had served as prefect of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 第進士，又以書判高等補秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and, by high rank in the document judgment test, was appointed corrector of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and, by high rank in the document judgment test, was appointed corrector of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李懷光辟致幕府，擢累監察御史。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang recruited him to his staff; he was promoted in succession to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang recruited him to his staff, and he rose in succession to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 懷光反河中，鄘與母、妻陷焉，因紿懷光以兄病臥洛且革，母欲往視；

translations.literal: When Huaiguang rebelled in Hezhong, Yong and his mother and wife were trapped there; he deceived Huaiguang, saying his elder brother lay ill in Luoyang and was near death and his mother wished to go see him;
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiguang rebelled in Hezhong, Yong and his mother and wife were trapped there; he deceived Huaiguang, saying his elder brother lay gravely ill in Luoyang and his mother wished to visit him;

sentences.zh: 懷光許可，戒妻子無偕行。

translations.literal: Huaiguang granted permission but warned that wife and children must not go together.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang agreed but warned that his wife and children must not travel together.

sentences.zh: 鄘私遣之，懷光怒，欲加罪，謝曰：「鄘籍在軍，不得為母駕，奈何不使婦往？」

translations.literal: Yong secretly sent them off; Huaiguang was angry and wished to punish him; Yong apologized, saying, "Yong is registered in the army and cannot escort his mother—how could I not let my wife go?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong secretly sent them off; Huaiguang was furious and wished to punish him; Yong apologized, saying, "I am registered in the army and cannot escort my mother—how could I not let my wife go?"

sentences.zh: 懷光止不問。

translations.literal: Huaiguang stopped and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 後與高郢刺賊虛實及所以攻取者，白諸朝，德宗手詔褒答。

translations.literal: Later, with Gao Ye, he investigated the rebels' strengths and weaknesses and how to attack and take them, reporting to the court; Dezong personally wrote an edict in praise and reply.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Gao Ye investigated the rebels' strengths and weaknesses and how to defeat them, reported to the court, and Dezong personally wrote an edict praising their work.

sentences.zh: 懷光覺，嚴兵召二人問之，鄘詞氣不撓，三軍為感動，懷光不殺，囚之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang discovered this, drew up troops strictly, and summoned the two to question them; Yong's tone did not bend, the whole army was moved, Huaiguang did not kill them but imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang discovered this, mobilized his troops, and summoned the two men to question them; Yong's bearing did not waver, the whole army was moved, and Huaiguang imprisoned them rather than execute them.

sentences.zh: 河中平，馬燧破械致禮，表佐其府，以言不用，罷歸洛中。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, Ma Sui removed their shackles and treated them with courtesy; Yong memorialized to serve on his staff; his counsel was not used and he was dismissed to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhong was pacified, Ma Sui released them and treated them with courtesy; Yong offered to serve on his staff, but when his counsel was ignored he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 徐州張建封卒，兵亂，囚監軍，迫建封子愔主軍務。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou died, the army mutinied, imprisoned the army supervisor, and forced Jianfeng's son Yin to take charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou died, the army mutinied, imprisoned the army supervisor, and forced Jianfeng's son Yin to take command.

sentences.zh: 帝以鄘剛敢，拜宣慰使，持節直入其軍，大會士，喻以禍福，出監軍獄中，脫桎梏，使復位，眾不敢動。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Yong firm and bold, appointed him pacification commissioner; bearing credentials he entered the army directly, convened the troops, explained gain and loss, brought the supervisor out of prison, removed his fetters, restored him to office, and none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, knowing Yong to be firm and bold, appointed him pacification commissioner; bearing imperial credentials he entered the camp, assembled the troops, explained the consequences of their actions, freed the supervisor from prison, restored him to office, and none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 愔即上表謝罪，稱兵馬留後，鄘曰：「非詔命，安得輒稱之？」

translations.literal: Yin at once memorialized confessing guilt and styled himself military affairs acting commissioner; Yong said, "Without an edict, how can you presume to use such a title?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin immediately memorialized confessing guilt and styled himself acting military commissioner; Yong said, "Without an imperial edict, how can you presume to use such a title?"

sentences.zh: 削去乃受。

translations.literal: Only when the title was struck out did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the improper title was removed did he accept the memorial.

sentences.zh: 既還，稱旨，遷郎中。

translations.literal: After his return he met the emperor's wishes and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he pleased the emperor and was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 順宗時，進御史中丞。

translations.literal: In Shunzong's time he advanced to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: During Shunzong's reign he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，為京兆尹，進尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When Xianzong acceded he became Intendant of the Capital and advanced to right vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong came to the throne he became Intendant of the Capital and was promoted to right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元和初，京師多盜賊，復拜京兆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe bandits were numerous in the capital; he was again appointed Intendant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign bandits were rife in the capital, and he was again appointed Intendant of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 以檢校禮部尚書為鳳翔、隴右節度使。

translations.literal: As acting minister of the Ministry of Rites he was made military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: As acting minister of rites he was appointed military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 是鎮常兼神策行營，前此用武將，始受詔，即詣軍脩謁。

translations.literal: This command regularly also held the Shence field army; before this military generals, upon first receiving the edict, at once went to the army to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: This command regularly also controlled the Shence field army; previously military generals, upon receiving their appointment, immediately went to the army to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 鄘以為不可，詔為去神策行營號。

translations.literal: Yong held this improper; an edict removed the Shence field army designation.
translations.idiomatic: Yong held this improper; an edict removed the Shence field army designation from his command.

sentences.zh: 俄徙河東，入為刑部尚書、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hedong; he entered the capital as minister of justice and transport commissioner for salt and iron of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Hedong, then recalled as minister of justice and transport commissioner for salt and iron of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 拜淮南節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 王師討蔡方急，李師道謀撓沮之，鄘以兵二萬分壁鄆境，貲餉不仰有司。

translations.literal: As imperial forces pressed the campaign against Cai, Li Shidao plotted to thwart it; Yong stationed twenty thousand troops along the border of Yan, and supplies and pay did not depend on the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial forces pressed the campaign against Cai, Li Shidao plotted to interfere; Yong stationed twenty thousand troops along the Yan border and supplied them from his own resources without relying on the central government.

sentences.zh: 是時兵興，天子憂財乏，使程异馳驛江淮，諷諸道輸貨助軍。

translations.literal: At this time war was underway and the Son of Heaven worried over lack of funds; he sent Cheng Yi by post relay to the Jianghuai region to hint that the circuits should submit goods to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: War was underway and the emperor worried over lack of funds; he sent Cheng Yi posthaste to the Jianghuai region to urge the circuits to contribute supplies for the army.

sentences.zh: 鄘素富強，即籍府庫留一歲儲，餘盡納於朝，諸道由是悉索以獻，繄鄘倡之。

translations.literal: Yong had long been wealthy and strong; he at once inventoried the treasury, kept one year's stores, and sent the rest entirely to the court; the circuits thereupon all searched out and presented contributions—it was Yong who initiated this.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's circuit had long been prosperous; he inventoried the treasury, kept one year's reserves, and sent the rest to the court; the other circuits thereupon all searched out contributions to present—it was Yong who led the way.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐突承璀為監軍，貴寵甚，鄘以剛嚴治，相禮憚，稍厚善。

translations.literal: Earlier Tutu Chenghui was army supervisor, greatly favored and petted; Yong governed with stern rigor; they mutually respected and feared each other and gradually became close.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tutu Chenghui served as army supervisor and was greatly favored; Yong governed with stern rigor; they came to respect and fear each other and gradually became friendly.

sentences.zh: 承璀歸，數稱薦之，召拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Chenghui returned to court he repeatedly praised and recommended him; Yong was summoned as vice director of the Chancellery and concurrent Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghui returned to court he repeatedly recommended Yong, who was summoned as vice director of the Chancellery and concurrent chancellor.

sentences.zh: 鄘不喜由宦幸進，及出祖，樂作泣下，謂諸將曰：「吾老安外鎮，宰相豈吾任乎？」

translations.literal: Yong disliked advancement through eunuch favor; at the farewell feast when music played he wept and said to the generals, "I am old and content in an outer command—how could the chancellorship be my post?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong disliked having advanced through eunuch favor; at his farewell feast, when the music played, he wept and said to his generals, "I am old and content as a frontier commander—how could the chancellorship be my place?"

sentences.zh: 至京師，不肯視事，引疾固辭，改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he refused to take up duties, pleaded illness and firmly declined, and was changed to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital he refused to take office, pleaded illness, and was reassigned minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校尚書左僕射，兼太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting left vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent guest of the heir apparent on detached duty in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting left vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent guest of the heir apparent on detached duty in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以太子少傅致仕，卒，贈太子太保，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He retired as junior tutor to the heir apparent; he died and was posthumously made grand tutor to the heir apparent, with posthumous title Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as junior tutor to the heir apparent; upon his death he was posthumously made grand tutor to the heir apparent, with the posthumous title Su (Solemn).

sentences.zh: 鄘強直無私，與楊憑、穆質、許孟容、王仲舒友善，皆以氣自任。

translations.literal: Yong was forceful, upright, and without private bias; he was friendly with Yang Ping, Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Wang Zhongshu—all took spirit as their charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was forceful, upright, and impartial; he was friendly with Yang Ping, Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, and Wang Zhongshu—all men who prided themselves on their integrity.

sentences.zh: 而鄘當官，以峭法操下，所至稱治。

translations.literal: In office Yong governed subordinates with stern law; wherever he went he was praised for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yong governed subordinates with stern discipline; wherever he served he was praised for good administration.

sentences.zh: 猛決少恩，在淮南七年，其生殺禽擿，多委軍吏，而參佐束手不得與，人往往陷非法，議者亦以此少之。

translations.literal: He was fierce in decision and sparing of grace; in Huainan for seven years, life, death, arrest, and seizure were mostly entrusted to army clerks, while staff assistants stood by unable to participate; people often fell into unlawful trouble, and critics for this reason thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce in judgment and sparing of mercy; during seven years in Huainan, decisions of life and death and arrests were mostly left to army officers while his staff could not intervene; many people suffered injustice, and critics held this against him.

sentences.zh: 子拭，仕歷宗正卿、京兆尹、河東鳳翔節度使，以秘書監卒。

translations.literal: His son Shi served as director of the Imperial Clan Court, Intendant of the Capital, and military commissioner of Hedong and Fengxiang, and died as director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi served as director of the Imperial Clan Court, Intendant of the Capital, and military commissioner of Hedong and Fengxiang, and died while serving as director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 拭子磎，字景望。

translations.literal: Shi's son Xi, courtesy name Jingwang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's son Xi, whose courtesy name was Jingwang.

sentences.zh: 大中末，擢進士，累遷戶部郎中，分司東都。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dazhong era he was selected jinshi and promoted in succession to director of the Bureau of Revenue on detached duty in the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dazhong reign he passed the jinshi examination and rose in succession to director of the Bureau of Revenue on detached duty in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 劾奏內園使郝景全不法事，景全反摘磎奏犯順宗嫌名，坐奪俸。

translations.literal: He impeached Inner Park Commissioner Hao Jingquan for unlawful conduct; Jingquan in turn seized on Xi's memorial for violating the taboo name of Shunzong, and Xi was punished by loss of salary.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Inner Park Commissioner Hao Jingquan for unlawful conduct; Jingquan in turn accused Xi's memorial of violating the taboo name of Emperor Shunzong, and Xi was punished by loss of salary.

sentences.zh: 磎上言：「『因事告事，旁訟他人』者，咸通詔語也。

translations.literal: Xi submitted, "'Reporting a matter by way of a matter and bringing a side suit against another person' is language from a Xiantong edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xi submitted, "The phrase 'reporting a matter by way of a matter and bringing a side suit against another person' comes from a Xiantong edict.

sentences.zh: 禮，不諱嫌名；

translations.literal: By ritual, taboo homophones are not avoided;
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, homophones of taboo names are not avoided;

sentences.zh: 律，廟諱嫌名不坐。

translations.literal: by law, violation of ancestral taboo homophones is not punishable.
translations.idiomatic: and by law, violation of ancestral taboo homophones is not punishable.

sentences.zh: 豈臣所引詔書而有司輒論奏？

translations.literal: How could the edict I cited be the basis for the relevant offices to judge and memorialize against me?
translations.idiomatic: How could the relevant offices prosecute me on the basis of the very edict I cited?

sentences.zh: 臣恐自今用格令者，委曲回避，旁緣為奸也。」

translations.literal: I fear that from now on those who apply regulations will twist and evade, using side pretexts to commit treachery."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that from now on those who apply regulations will twist them to evade justice and use side pretexts to commit wrongdoing."

sentences.zh: 詔不奪俸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that his salary not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that his salary not be forfeited.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷洛，磎挾尚書八印走河陽，時留守劉允章為賊脅，遣人就磎索印，拒不與。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took Luoyang, Xi carried off eight seals of the Secretariat and fled to Heyang; the acting commander Liu Yunzhang was coerced by the bandits and sent someone to demand the seals from Xi; he refused to give them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Luoyang, Xi carried off eight seals of the Secretariat and fled to Heyang; the acting commander Liu Yunzhang had been coerced by the rebels and sent someone to demand the seals; Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 允章悟，亦不臣賊。

translations.literal: Yunzhang understood and also did not submit to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhang took the hint and also refused to submit to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 嗣襄王之亂，轉側淮南，高駢受偽命，磎苦諫，不納。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of the Prince of Xiang's succession, moving about in Huainan, Gao Pian accepted a false commission; Xi remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil over the succession of the Prince of Xiang, as events shifted in Huainan, Gao Pian accepted a false imperial commission; Xi remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 入為中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He entered office as drafting secretary of the Secretariat and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as drafting secretary of the Secretariat and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 辭職歸華陰，復以學士召。

translations.literal: He resigned and returned to Huayin, then was again summoned as academician.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and returned to Huayin, then was summoned again as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年，進禮部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianning, he was promoted to minister of rites and concurrent chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianning he was promoted to minister of rites and concurrent chancellor.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯素疾磎，諷劉崇魯掠其麻哭之，言：「磎懷奸，與中人楊復恭昵款，其弟為時溥所殺，不可相天子。」

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei had long resented Xi and prompted Liu Chonglu to snatch his appointment edict and weep over it, saying, "Xi harbors treachery, is on familiar terms with the eunuch Yang Fugong, and his younger brother was killed by Shi Bo—he must not serve as chancellor to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei had long resented Xi and prompted Liu Chonglu to snatch his appointment edict and weep over it, saying, "Xi harbors treachery, is on familiar terms with the eunuch Yang Fugong, and his younger brother was killed by Shi Bo—he must not serve as chancellor to the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 翌日，下遷太子少傅。

translations.literal: The next day an edict demoted him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict demoted him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 磎乃自言為崇魯誣汙，書十一上不止。

translations.literal: Xi then declared himself slandered by Chonglu and submitted memorial after memorial—eleven in all without cessation.
translations.idiomatic: Xi then declared himself slandered by Chonglu and submitted memorial after memorial—eleven in all without stopping.

sentences.zh: 初，崇魯父坐受賕，仰藥死，故磎以醜語及之，議者譏其非大臣體。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chonglu's father had been convicted of accepting bribes and died by taking poison; therefore Xi brought up ugly words about this, and critics mocked him for failing to comport himself as a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chonglu's father had been convicted of accepting bribes and died by taking poison; Xi therefore brought up ugly words about this, and critics mocked him for failing to comport himself as a great minister.

sentences.zh: 昭宗素所器遇，決意復用之，而李茂貞等上言深詆其非，帝不獲已，又罷為太子少師。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong had long valued him and resolved to restore him to office, but Li Maozhen and others submitted memorials bitterly denouncing him; the emperor had no choice and again dismissed him as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong had long valued him and resolved to restore him to office, but Li Maozhen and others submitted memorials bitterly denouncing him; the emperor had no choice and again dismissed him as Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 於是茂貞及王行瑜、韓建擁兵闕下，列磎罪，殺之於都亭驛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Maozhen together with Wang Xingyu and Han Jian massed troops below the palace gates, listed Xi's crimes, and killed him at the Duting Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Maozhen together with Wang Xingyu and Han Jian massed troops below the palace gates, listed Xi's crimes, and killed him at the Duting Post Station.

sentences.zh: 行瑜誅，有詔復官爵，贈司徒，謚曰文。

translations.literal: After Xingyu was executed, an edict restored Xi's office and rank, posthumously made him Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyu was executed, an edict restored Xi's office and rank, posthumously made him Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 磎好學，家有書至萬卷，世號「李書樓」。

translations.literal: Xi loved learning; his household had books reaching ten thousand scrolls, and the age called him "Li the Book Tower."
translations.idiomatic: Xi loved learning; his household held ten thousand scrolls of books, and he was known as "Li the Book Tower."

sentences.zh: 所著文章及註解諸書傳甚多。

translations.literal: His essays and commentaries on various classics and histories were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote extensively, including many commentaries on the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 子沇，字東濟，有俊才，亦遇害，贈禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Yan, courtesy name Dongji, had outstanding talent, also met with violent death, and was posthumously made vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, courtesy name Dongji, had outstanding talent, also met a violent death, and was posthumously made vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：剛者天德，故孔子稱「剛近仁」。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Firmness is Heaven's virtue; therefore Confucius said "firmness is close to benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Firmness is Heaven's virtue; therefore Confucius said that "firmness is close to benevolence."

sentences.zh: 骨強四支，故君有忠臣，謂之骨鯁。

translations.literal: When the bones are strong in the four limbs, the ruler has loyal ministers—called bone spurs in the throat.
translations.idiomatic: When the bones are strong in the four limbs, the ruler has loyal ministers—men called the bone in the throat.

sentences.zh: 若棲筠、鄘二子，其剛者歟！

translations.literal: Of Qiyun and Yong, these two men—were they not the firm ones!
translations.idiomatic: Of Qiyun and Yong, these two men—were they not men of firmness!

sentences.zh: 棲筠抗權邪，不及相；

translations.literal: Qiyun resisted powerful wrongdoers but did not reach the chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun resisted the powerful and corrupt but never became chancellor;

sentences.zh: 鄘得相，不願拜。

translations.literal: Yong received the chancellorship but did not wish to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was offered the chancellorship but did not wish to accept it.

sentences.zh: 非剛，疇克勝之？

translations.literal: Without firmness, who could have overcome these things?
translations.idiomatic: Without firmness, who could have accomplished these things?

sentences.zh: 吉甫踐天宰，謀謨是矣，而鯁正有愧於父雲。

translations.literal: Jifu trod the seat of Heaven's minister and his planning and counsel were right, yet in bone-spur uprightness he had cause to feel ashamed before his father.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu held the highest office and his counsel was sound, yet in the bone-spur uprightness of a loyal remonstrator he fell short of his father.
